l: Bihagre ki War, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Bihagre ki War
s: Bihagre ki War says that the Hindus have forgotten God and are going the wrong way. It describes their worship of stones and questions how a sinking stone could carry them across.

l: Hindus, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Bihagre ki War
s: The Hindus are described as having forgotten God and following the wrong way. They worship according to the instruction of Narad, are called blind and dumb, and take stones to worship them.

l: God, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Bihagre ki War
s: God is described as having been forgotten by the Hindus.

l: Hymns of Guru Nanak, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Wadhans .. Wadhans ki War
s: Rag Wadhans concerns a fervent woman who longs for God, grieves separation from the Beloved, and is willing to sacrifice herself in service. Wadhans Chhant teaches that truth, God's word, and God's name are superior to ritual washing, alms, and other good works, while human life and happiness come according to God's will and past acts. Wadhans Alahanian says that God created and governs the world, is present in every heart, and is known through the Guru's instruction and meditation on the Name. Wadhans ki War declares that ritual is worthless when it causes a person to forget the Beloved, while true love preserves honour with God.

l: Rag Wadhans, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Wadhans .. Wadhans ki War
s: Rag Wadhans presents the fervent woman's longing for God and the Beloved. She decorates herself but is not accepted, mourns separation, seeks to see God in dreams, and offers her head and life in service.

l: Wadhans Chhant, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Wadhans .. Wadhans ki War
s: Wadhans Chhant teaches that truth in the heart is the acceptable ablution and that God's word and name bring happiness. It says that God grants human life according to past acts, that people should avoid quarrels and jealousy, and that God's name is greater than alms and good works.

l: Wadhans Alahanian, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Wadhans .. Wadhans ki War
s: Wadhans Alahanian says that God created the world and drew it within Himself. God is present in every heart and is known through the Guru's instruction and meditation on the Name.

l: Wadhans ki War, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Wadhans .. Wadhans ki War
s: Wadhans ki War declares that ritual should perish when it causes a person to forget the Beloved. It identifies true love as that which preserves a person in honour with God.

l: God, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Wadhans .. Wadhans ki War
s: God is described as the Master, Creator, Beloved, and True One. God grants human life according to past acts, gives happiness and sorrow, is present in every heart, and does as He pleases.

l: the Name, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Wadhans .. Wadhans ki War
s: God's name is described as ambrosial and sweet to the soul. It brings happiness, removes sorrow, grants victory in the arena of the world, and is superior to alms-offerings and various good works.

l: fervent woman, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Wadhans .. Wadhans ki War
s: The fervent woman is enamoured of God's glances and longs for the Beloved. She is not accepted despite her decorations, weeps in separation, wishes to see God in dreams, and offers her head and life in service.

l: world, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Wadhans .. Wadhans ki War
s: The world was created by God, who looks on all things with favour and knows its ways. God spread the net of mammon through the world, and people desire what is sweet rather than bitter.

l: truth, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Wadhans .. Wadhans ki War
s: Truth is presented as the acceptable ablution for a body defiled by falsehood. When truth is in the heart, a person becomes true and obtains the True One.

l: God's love, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Wadhans .. Wadhans ki War
s: Love is true when it preserves a person in honour with God. Ritual is condemned when it causes a person to forget the Beloved.

l: Hymns of Guru Nanak, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Sorath .. Sorath Ashtapadi
s: Rag Sorath teaches that death, destiny, and separation come to all creatures, while God alone is beyond death and destiny. It urges humanity to praise God, repeat God's Name and Word, serve the Guru and True Guru, abandon mammon, and cultivate virtue. Sorath Ashtapadi describes the Bairagi as one who renounces desire, remains absorbed in God's love, and treasures the Word at home. It also teaches that Pandit learning and religious ceremonies are worthless without meditation, the Guru's instruction, and the Name.

l: Rag Sorath, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Sorath .. Sorath Ashtapadi
s: Rag Sorath teaches that all must die and part, that those who forget God suffer, and that God alone is the Benefactor. It praises God's greatness and urges humanity to repeat God's Name, serve the Guru, and seek protection so the soul may blend with the Supreme Soul.

l: Sorath Ashtapadi, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Sorath .. Sorath Ashtapadi
s: Sorath Ashtapadi teaches resistance to mammon, rejection of empty rituals, and devotion to God through the Guru's instruction. It describes the Bairagi, the Pandit, destiny, and the power of God's Name to free humanity from doubt and transmigration.

l: God, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Sorath .. Sorath Ashtapadi
s: God is described as unseen, infinite, inaccessible, inapprehensible, unborn, self-existent, fearless, and beyond death and destiny. God is present in every heart, grants wisdom and divine knowledge, directs all acts, and alone gives happiness, greatness, and liberation.

l: Nanak, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Sorath .. Sorath Ashtapadi
s: Nanak teaches that humanity's sins become chains, while virtues cut those chains off. Nanak praises God, identifies himself as the slave of slaves, and says that the Guru's teaching reveals God and makes a person a perfect Bairagi.

l: Guru, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Sorath .. Sorath Ashtapadi
s: The Guru unites humanity with God, gives the water of life, purifies the heart, and teaches the Name. Meeting the Guru produces understanding, removes doubt and fear, and shows the way to true peace and release from transmigration.

l: Guru, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Sorath .. Sorath Ashtapadi
s: The True Guru is the source of the real boon and ambrosial Name. Serving the True Guru brings happiness, divine knowledge, steadfastness in God's service, freedom from hypocrisy, and release from transmigration.

l: the Name, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Sorath .. Sorath Ashtapadi
s: God's Name is the support and capital that brings happiness, purity, contentment, and freedom from doubt. Repeating it under the Guru's instruction destroys greed, protects from transmigration, and is superior to ablutions, alms, and similar religious acts.

l: the Word, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Sorath .. Sorath Ashtapadi
s: The Word manifests God, penetrates the heart, and is treasured by the true Bairagi. The Word, received through the Guru's instruction, helps purify the heart and leads to divine understanding.

l: mammon, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Sorath .. Sorath Ashtapadi
s: Mammon causes greed, worldly attachment, error, and spiritual ruin. The text teaches that devotion to mammon cannot obtain the water of life and that humanity must abandon mammon and its entanglements.

l: Death, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Sorath .. Sorath Ashtapadi
s: Death comes to all creatures, and God has made animals subject to death. Those who forget God or breathe in vain without Him die without spiritual support, while singing God's praises removes the fear of birth and death.

l: destiny, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Sorath .. Sorath Ashtapadi
s: Destiny governs all creatures from the beginning, with each animal bearing its destined record on its forehead. God alone is not subject to destiny and causes His order to be executed.

l: man, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Sorath .. Sorath Ashtapadi
s: Humanity is subject to death, destiny, sin, greed, falsehood, and transmigration, but can obtain happiness and liberation through God's Name, the Guru, virtue, and service. Humanity is taught to regard all people as equal because God's light is in every heart.

l: Bairagis, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Sorath .. Sorath Ashtapadi
s: A Bairagi is not merely one who adopts an outward identity but one who abandons desire, treasures the Word, fears God, serves the Guru, and remains absorbed in divine pleasure. The perfect Bairagi is pleasing to God, content with the Name, and naturally fortunate.

l: Pandit, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Sorath .. Sorath Ashtapadi
s: The Pandit is criticized for chattering about the Shastars and Veds while treating them as a worldly affair. The text teaches the Pandit that meditation on the Supreme Being, rather than hypocrisy or empty learning, is the religious practice that brings happiness.

l: religious ceremonies, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Sorath .. Sorath Ashtapadi
s: Religious ceremonies, hopes, and desires are called entanglements when performed without devotion and understanding. The text says they are worthless without meditation on the Supreme Being, and that the Name is superior to ablutions, alms, and similar acts.

l: Hymns of Guru Nanak, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Dhanasari .. Dhanasari Chhant
s: Rag Dhanasari concerns devotion to God, reliance on God's name, human mortality, destiny, moral conduct, and the true religious life. It teaches that Nanak serves God, that people receive the fruits of their own actions, and that deceit leads toward death. It contrasts genuine spiritual conduct with the failings of the Qazi, Brahman, and Jogi, and describes the virtues of one who recognizes and serves the One. Dhanasari Ashtapadi emphasizes love and service to God, while Dhanasari Chhant describes a woman seeking honour by pleasing her Spouse.

l: Rag Dhanasari, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Dhanasari .. Dhanasari Chhant
s: Rag Dhanasari teaches reliance on God, service to Him, remembrance of God's name, acceptance of destiny, and accountability for actions. It contrasts true devotion with deceit and empty religious practices.

l: Dhanasari Ashtapadi, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Dhanasari .. Dhanasari Chhant
s: Dhanasari Ashtapadi teaches that God is satisfied by human love and service, not obstinate penance or religious garb. It says that remembrance of God's name leads to piety and absorption in God, while stone worship, pilgrimage, forest dwelling, and renunciation do not purify a filthy mind.

l: Dhanasari Chhant, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Dhanasari .. Dhanasari Chhant
s: Dhanasari Chhant says that a woman who pleases her Spouse is honoured in His house. A woman who utters falsehood is not regarded by her Spouse and suffers painful nights.

l: God, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Dhanasari .. Dhanasari Chhant
s: God is the Giver, ever young, merciful, and the one True Being without a second. He knows people's secrets, grants favour, determines what they obtain, and is satisfied by love and service.

l: Nanak, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Dhanasari .. Dhanasari Chhant
s: Nanak calls himself God's slave and an eternal sacrifice to Him. He teaches service to God, remembrance of God's name, acceptance of destiny, and that people receive the fruit of their own actions.

l: man, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Dhanasari .. Dhanasari Chhant
s: Humanity lives only briefly and does not know how long life will last. People are taught to serve God, remember Him, act truthfully, and understand that their actions determine their reward.

l: the Name, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Dhanasari .. Dhanasari Chhant
s: God's name enables people to cross over, remain attached to God, and become absorbed in Him. Those who forget it despite reading and cleverness suffer punishment and transmigration.

l: thief, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Dhanasari .. Dhanasari Chhant
s: The thief's praise or reviling cannot affect the magistrate, and nobody will stand surety for him. However well dressed or ingenious, the thief is counterfeit, receives the fruit of his actions, and is known by the True One.

l: the Qazi, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Dhanasari .. Dhanasari Chhant
s: The Qazi is condemned when he tells lies and eats filth. A true Qazi turns people away from the world and, by the Guru's favour, is dead while alive.

l: Brahman, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Dhanasari .. Dhanasari Chhant
s: The Brahman is condemned when he takes life and then bathes. A true Brahman reflects upon God and is saved himself while saving all his relations.

l: Jogi, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Dhanasari .. Dhanasari Chhant
s: The ignorant Jogi does not know the way to union with God and helps ruin the world. A true Jogi knows the way to God and recognizes the One by the Guru's favour.

l: Musalman, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Dhanasari .. Dhanasari Chhant
s: A Musalman is described as one who cleanses his impurity.

l: woman, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Dhanasari .. Dhanasari Chhant
s: The woman is described as seeking honour in her Spouse's house by pleasing Him. If she speaks falsely, she is forgotten by her Spouse and experiences painful nights.

l: Spouse, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Dhanasari .. Dhanasari Chhant
s: The Spouse honours a woman who pleases Him but does not look at one who utters falsehood.

l: world, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Dhanasari .. Dhanasari Chhant
s: The world is a place where people should hear and speak of God while they live. It is also said to be ruined by the ignorant Jogi, the lying Qazi, and the life-taking Brahman.

l: Death, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Dhanasari .. Dhanasari Chhant
s: Death is the destination to whose gate the deceitful person is led captive. The deceitful person regrets lost opportunities when being led there.

l: destiny, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Dhanasari .. Dhanasari Chhant
s: Destiny is written on the forehead and engraved in God's court. What is counterfeit is of no avail, and whoever is destined from the beginning to obtain something shall obtain it.

l: Hymns of Guru Nanak, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Suhi .. Suhi ki War
s: This unit presents Rag Suhi, Suhi Ashtapadi, Suhi Chhant, and Suhi ki War as teachings on devotion, divine knowledge, moral conduct, and union with God. It describes man as wandering through attachment, passion, falsehood, and transmigration unless he serves God, follows the Guru, and embraces the Name and the Word. Nanak teaches that God tests deeds, protects those devoted to Him, pardons the loving, and grants liberation. The unit also contrasts genuine spiritual understanding with empty ritual, including bathing, reading the Veds, and outward religious display.

l: Rag Suhi, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Suhi .. Suhi ki War
s: Rag Suhi teaches that man should not forsake ambrosia for poison or remain bound by worldly entanglements. It praises service to the True One and says that recognizing oneself as neither good nor bad brings salvation.

l: Suhi Ashtapadi, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Suhi .. Suhi ki War
s: Suhi Ashtapadi describes the soul as a bride lacking beauty, merit, wisdom, and good conduct, yet capable of pleasing the Spouse through divine knowledge, humility, and devotion. It teaches that attachment to mammon causes loss, while love of the True One prevents rebirth and leads to union with the Beloved.

l: Suhi Chhant, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Suhi .. Suhi ki War
s: Suhi Chhant celebrates the arrival of the Spouse and the saints, whose presence brings happiness, nectar, divine knowledge, and the jewel of love. It teaches that the Guru removes the soul's misery and that longing, love, and remembrance lead the mind home to the True One.

l: Suhi ki War, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Suhi .. Suhi ki War
s: Suhi ki War teaches that God tests the genuine and counterfeit in the divine court and condemns hypocrisy, falsehood, empty ritual, and irreligious company. It praises the Name and God's praises above ritual calls, Vedic reading without understanding, and outward cleansing.

l: Nanak, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Suhi .. Suhi ki War
s: Nanak teaches that service, humility, love, remembrance of the Name, and acceptance of the Guru's instruction lead to salvation. He says that God tests accounts, pardons those who love the True One, and blends the liberated with Himself.

l: God, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Suhi .. Suhi ki War
s: God is described as the True One, the Benefactor, the Creator, the Dispenser of weal and woe, and the source of light and divine knowledge. God protects, tests, pardons, grants liberation, and is found through love.

l: Guru, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Suhi .. Suhi ki War
s: The Guru gives God's dye, protects those who follow him, and provides instruction that can save man. The Guru also removes the soul's misery and is necessary for obtaining divine knowledge.

l: man, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Suhi .. Suhi ki War
s: Man wanders through attachment, passion, falsehood, pleasure, and transmigration, often forgetting the Creator. He is saved by service, love for the True One, the Name, the Word, good fortune, and the Guru's instruction.

l: saints, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Suhi .. Suhi ki War
s: The saints bring happiness when they come to the house, causing the soul and home to appear bright. Meeting them is associated with rejoicing, divine knowledge, and spiritual fulfillment.

l: Pandits, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Suhi .. Suhi ki War
s: The Pandits claim that reading the Veds dispels sinful inclinations, but the teaching says that reading the Veds without understanding is only a secular occupation. They are warned that those who do not delight in the Word or love God's Name will be disgraced.

l: divine knowledge, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Suhi .. Suhi ki War
s: Divine knowledge is presented as the means by which man becomes a servant of the True One and mental ignorance is dispelled. It is obtained through the Guru and is symbolized as salve that enables one to see God's form.

l: the Name, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Suhi .. Suhi ki War
s: The Name is the support of the supportless and the means by which man profits spiritually and avoids wandering in error. It is superior to ritual calls and is necessary for love, salvation, and freedom from rebirth.

l: the Word, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Suhi .. Suhi ki War
s: The Word saves those who listen to the Guru's instruction and removes demerits. Those who lack the Word and do not fear God are watched by the god of death.

l: mammon, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Suhi .. Suhi ki War
s: Mammon causes people to become absorbed in superstition, false pride, and worldly attachment. Those who make mammon their friend are lost and ultimately die and blend with dust.

l: transmigration, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Suhi .. Suhi ki War
s: Transmigration follows when man is led astray by the various phases of life and by the effects of good and evil acts. It ends through God's favouring glance and union with God.

l: death, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Suhi .. Suhi ki War
s: Birth and death produce misery and separation from God. Beholding the Spouse ends the pain of birth and death.

l: God's love, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Suhi .. Suhi ki War
s: Love is the means by which God is found and brings the soul home to the True One. The jewel of love fills the heart, while the absence of true love turns love into hate.

l: the True Guru's instruction, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Suhi .. Suhi ki War
s: God's instruction adjusts the affairs of the soul and enables it to see God's form. Those who follow the Guru's instruction are saved.

l: the Veds, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Suhi .. Suhi ki War
s: The Veds are read by the Pandits, but the unit says that reading them without understanding does not dispel mental ignorance and is merely a secular occupation.

l: house, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Suhi .. Suhi ki War
s: The house becomes bright and spiritually joyful when saints arrive, and it is adorned when the Spouse comes. The empty house represents those who leave without obtaining the sweets of love or the Bridegroom's delights.

l: world, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Suhi .. Suhi ki War
s: The world is pervaded by God, yet it wanders bound by its own entanglements and forgets the Creator. Its people are compared to transient shopkeepers engaged in worldly traffic.

l: Hymns of Guru Nanak, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Bilawal
s: Rag Bilawal is a devotional hymn in which Nanak praises God as the source of all things and the object of complete devotion. Nanak asks God for understanding to sing His praises and admits that he cannot describe the Indescribable. He presents himself as a foolish, blind, strange dog who survives by barking for his belly, yet still bears his Master's name. He describes his body as a Qalandar's dress, his heart as a temple, and his soul as pierced by the Compassionate One.

l: Rag Bilawal, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Bilawal
s: Rag Bilawal presents Nanak's praise and devotion to God. It describes Nanak's humility, his inability to comprehend or describe God fully, and his efforts to make his heart a temple and avoid being born again.

l: God, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Bilawal
s: God is described as the emperor, lord, source of all things, and lover of all. God is inaccessible, imperceptible, unseen, boundless, and present as light in every heart. God provides protection, understanding, compassion, and care for all beings, and what pleases God is considered good.

l: Nanak, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Bilawal
s: Nanak calls himself foolish, blind, and unable to describe God, asking God to give him understanding to sing praises truthfully. He says he thinks of no one but God, has made his heart a temple, and will not be born again because the one word dwells in his heart. Although he performs no service, he still bears his Master's name.

l: Hymns of Guru Nanak, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Lunar Days
s: The unit concerns repeating the Name of the Lord of the world under the Guru's instruction. It teaches that attachment to mammon leads people to Death's gate, suffering, and transmigration, while no one is emancipated without the Guru's instruction. On the tenth day of the lunar month, people are told to repeat the Name as offerings and ablutions and to immerse themselves in the attributes and knowledge of the True One. When doubts and fears depart, the true heart is free of impurity, and fixing the mind on the True One brings happiness.

l: Lord of the three worlds, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Lunar Days
s: The Lord of the world is the name that should be repeated.

l: Guru, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Lunar Days
s: The Guru's instruction enables people to see God's court in their own home.

l: God, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Lunar Days
s: God's court is seen in one's own home under the Guru's instruction.

l: Death, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Lunar Days
s: Death receives those attached to mammon at Death's gate, where they suffer transmigration and receive blows on the head from the god of death.

l: the True Guru's instruction, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Lunar Days
s: The Guru's instruction reveals God's court in one's own home and is necessary for emancipation.

l: the tenth day of the lunar month, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Lunar Days
s: The tenth day of the lunar month is a time to repeat the Name as offerings and ablutions.

l: the Name, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Lunar Days
s: The Name is to be repeated as offerings and ablutions on the tenth day of the lunar month.

l: God, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Lunar Days
s: The True One's attributes and knowledge are to be lived in day and night. Fixing the mind firmly on the True One brings happiness.

l: world, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Lunar Days
s: The world is compared to a frail cord that will soon snap.

l: Hymns of Guru Nanak, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Ramkali .. Ramkali ki War I
s: This unit concerns Ramkali, Ramkali ki War I, and teachings about God, the Guru, the Name, good works, truth, and salvation. It contrasts genuine devotion and meditation with hypocrisy, pride, worldly love, mammon, and sin among Jogis, Qazis, Brahmans, Musalmans, and others. It teaches that all people face death, judgment, and possible transmigration, while those who follow the Guru's instruction and remember the Name may obtain divine knowledge, peace, and salvation. Nanak describes the True Guru's instruction as the way to recognize God's will and live truthfully.

l: Ramkali, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Ramkali .. Ramkali ki War I
s: Ramkali presents teachings on devotion to God, the Name, meditation, good works, and the Guru's instruction. It describes the dangers of mammon, pride, worldly love, sin, and hypocrisy, and teaches that salvation comes through devotion and remembrance.

l: Ramkali ki War I, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Ramkali .. Ramkali ki War I
s: Ramkali ki War I criticizes religious hypocrisy among Gurus, Qazis, Brahmans, Musalmans, Jogis, and others. It teaches that truth, good works, remembrance of the Name, and service to God matter more than outward practices.

l: God, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Ramkali .. Ramkali ki War I
s: God is described as the primal, infinite, effulgent Being who gives the Name, judges all accounts, sends and recalls people, and may pardon them. God grants divine knowledge, peace, salvation, and other blessings to those who follow the Guru's instruction.

l: Nanak, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Ramkali .. Ramkali ki War I
s: Nanak teaches that the Name, devotion to God, good works, truth, and the Guru's instruction lead to salvation. He warns against pride, mammon, worldly love, hypocrisy, and dependence on outward religious practices.

l: Guru, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Ramkali .. Ramkali ki War I
s: The Guru gives instruction through which a person recognizes God's will, obtains understanding, and receives God's protection. The Guru's favour supports the Name and leads a person toward salvation.

l: Jogis, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Ramkali .. Ramkali ki War I
s: The Jogi is criticized for begging, hypocrisy, worldly attachment, and relying on outward marks such as ashes, patched coats, bags, and earrings. The Jogi who follows the Guru's instruction, practices meditation, and is content with the alms of love can live peacefully and see all people equally.

l: the Word, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Ramkali .. Ramkali ki War I
s: The Word is presented as a source of divine knowledge, truth, and freedom from pride and transmigration. Meditation on the Word brightens a person and helps him obtain God's abode.

l: the Name, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Ramkali .. Ramkali ki War I
s: The Name is the highest religious work and assists a person at the last hour. Remembering the Name saves a person from error, transmigration, and hell, while forgetting it leads to suffering.

l: mammon, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Ramkali .. Ramkali ki War I
s: Mammon draws the mind in every direction and causes people to forget the Name. Those tinctured with mammon do not reach God's mansion.

l: world, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Ramkali .. Ramkali ki War I
s: The world is described as a place where people amass wealth despite death, become intoxicated with wealth and worldly love, and face judgment for their deeds. The world also contains the entanglements from which the Guru's instruction can free a person.

l: transmigration, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Ramkali .. Ramkali ki War I
s: Transmigration follows from forgetfulness of the Name, worldly attachment, sin, and failure to follow the Guru's instruction. Holy people who know God and those who receive the Guru's favour can end transmigration and become absorbed in God.

l: salvation, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Ramkali .. Ramkali ki War I
s: Salvation is not obtained through outward austerities, ablutions, calculations, disguises, or religious claims alone. It is obtained through God's Name, the Guru's instruction, good works, truth, and devotion.

l: divine knowledge, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Ramkali .. Ramkali ki War I
s: Divine knowledge is a good material for the enduring lamp of devotion and is necessary for emancipation. Without it, outward practices and religious displays cannot save a person.

l: virtue, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Ramkali .. Ramkali ki War I
s: Good works are necessary for heaven, salvation, honour, and freedom from punishment. They are contrasted with sin, hypocrisy, and empty religious observances.

l: meditation, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Ramkali .. Ramkali ki War I
s: Meditation on the Name, the Word, and the Guru's instruction supports devotion and salvation. The Jogi who receives the alms of contemplation can overcome worldly pain.

l: truth, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Ramkali .. Ramkali ki War I
s: Truth is obtained through practicing truth, and false pride is condemned. Truth shall ultimately prevail when falsehood ends.

l: pride, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Ramkali .. Ramkali ki War I
s: Pride arises from beauty, wealth, status, and religious display and causes suffering and error. It departs through the Word and the Guru's instruction.

l: worldly love, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Ramkali .. Ramkali ki War I
s: Worldly love attaches people to gold, woman, wealth, houses, and sensual pleasures. It intoxicates the mind, causes anxiety and entanglement, and must be overcome through the Guru's instruction.

l: sin, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Ramkali .. Ramkali ki War I
s: Sin is committed by those who neglect truth, virtue, self-restraint, and the Name while pretending to be good. Sin brings punishment at death and cannot be erased by outward washing alone.

l: death, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Ramkali .. Ramkali ki War I
s: Death comes for everyone, takes people away when God calls them, and brings judgment for their deeds. At death, wealth, family, status, and possessions do not accompany a person.

l: the True Guru's instruction, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Ramkali .. Ramkali ki War I
s: The True Guru's instruction teaches people to recognize God's will, speak truth, abandon pride, and understand that God is present in every heart. Following it brings protection, happiness, divine knowledge, salvation, and absorption in the True One.

l: Hymns of Guru Nanak, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Maru Ashtapadi .. Maru ki War I
s: The unit concerns Rag Maru Ashtapadi, Maru Solhe, and Maru ki War I, describing God, the Guru, the True Name, and the way to emancipation. It condemns hypocritical religious practices, pride, avarice, lust, slander, and attachment to the world, while praising devotion, humility, truthful conduct, and service to the Guru. It teaches that the Guru's instruction and God's love save people from transmigration and lead them to God's court. Nanak presents the Guru, divine knowledge, true merchandise, and remembrance of God's Name as the means of crossing the world's terrible ocean.

l: Rag Maru Ashtapadi, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Maru Ashtapadi .. Maru ki War I
s: It teaches that hypocritical Sanyasis, householders, Jogis, and Kaparis who lack the Guru's instruction remain attached to greed, lust, pride, and superstition. It praises the true Sanyasi who serves the True Guru, subdues the passions with God's Name, and fixes attention on God's feet.

l: Maru Solhe, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Maru Ashtapadi .. Maru ki War I
s: It teaches that God is inaccessible and unfathomable, but is found through the true Guru's instruction, devotion, and remembrance of the Name. It describes the consequences of false dealings, attachment to mammon, and forgetting God, and praises those who pursue truth and carry on true traffic.

l: Maru ki War I, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Maru Ashtapadi .. Maru ki War I
s: It teaches that creation occurs by God's order and that God will call people to account for their love, conduct, and state of heart. It says that pride, doubt, fear, and transmigration depart through the Guru's wisdom and remembrance of God's Name.

l: God, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Maru Ashtapadi .. Maru ki War I
s: God created and sustains the world, knows the secrets of hearts, and speaks through wind, water, and fire. God grants emancipation, saves through the true Guru, judges people in God's court, and is found through devotion and the Name.

l: Guru, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Maru Ashtapadi .. Maru ki War I
s: The Guru is compared to a lake containing jewels and is the giver and procurer of emancipation. The Guru's instruction dispels pride, doubt, fear, and wandering, reveals God, and leads people to the Name and God's court.

l: Nanak, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Maru Ashtapadi .. Maru ki War I
s: Nanak teaches that the Name, the Guru, humility, truthful conduct, and God's love are the true means of salvation. He asks God to grant truth, preserve his honour, and cause people to meet the true Guru.

l: Sanyasi, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Maru Ashtapadi .. Maru ki War I
s: The true Sanyasi thinks of the one God under the Guru's instruction, loves His Name, and is satisfied with it. A hypocritical Sanyasi merely wears religious dress, begs, hoards money, and remains ignorant of the Word.

l: the pious, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Maru Ashtapadi .. Maru ki War I
s: Pious people carry on their dealings according to God's will, keep their true capital intact, and escape Death's noose. Their minds restrain wandering, and they are not punished by Death or forced onto the difficult road.

l: apostate, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Maru Ashtapadi .. Maru ki War I
s: The apostate forgets the Name, follows error and evil passions, and undergoes pain, transmigration, and bondage according to his acts. The apostate cannot obtain knowledge of the Word without the Guru.

l: woman, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Maru Ashtapadi .. Maru ki War I
s: The devotee woman separated from God suffers impatience and longing, but the woman who remembers the Beloved and finds Him through the Guru obtains peace. She is compared to a wife whose true Husband never forsakes those imbued with love of the True One.

l: the Name, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Maru Ashtapadi .. Maru ki War I
s: The True Name brings happiness, final deliverance, emancipation, and a sight of God's court. Repeating and reverencing it gives patience, removes fear and avarice, and prevents rebirth.

l: the Word, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Maru Ashtapadi .. Maru ki War I
s: The Guru's word is to be accepted as true and taught to the heart. It gives knowledge of God, dispels doubts and pride, and leads to absorption in God.

l: God's love, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Maru Ashtapadi .. Maru ki War I
s: God's love makes people fearless, peaceful, and detached from worldly desires. Those imbued with it are not separated from their Spouse and are led toward emancipation.

l: divine knowledge, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Maru Ashtapadi .. Maru ki War I
s: Divine knowledge enables a person to see the One who sees all things and to understand God under the Guru's instruction. Without it, religious appearances and learned texts do not reveal the Real Thing.

l: transmigration, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Maru Ashtapadi .. Maru ki War I
s: Transmigration results from forgetting the Name, evil actions, attachment to mammon, and ignorance of the Word. It ends through the Guru's instruction, God's love, humility, and remembrance of the Name.

l: emancipation, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Maru Ashtapadi .. Maru ki War I
s: Emancipation cannot be obtained without the true Guru and devotion to the primal God. The Guru grants and procures it, while love of God, truthful living, and the Name lead people to it.

l: Death, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Maru Ashtapadi .. Maru ki War I
s: Death acts as a tax-gatherer and binds people according to their deeds. Those who remember God's Name under the Guru's teaching are beyond Death's punishment, while others face its noose and the difficult road.

l: God's court, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Maru Ashtapadi .. Maru ki War I
s: God's court is reached by carrying the true merchandise of God's Name and living according to the Guru's instruction. Those who are emancipated receive a robe of honour there.

l: true merchandise, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Maru Ashtapadi .. Maru ki War I
s: True merchandise consists in truth, God's Name, and conduct according to God's will. Those who trade in it obtain profit, keep their capital intact, and reach God's court.

l: world, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Maru Ashtapadi .. Maru ki War I
s: The world is described as a terrible ocean in which people wander, suffer, and become attached to mammon. The Guru's instruction and dispelling the heart's doubts enable people to cross it.

l: religious life, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Maru Ashtapadi .. Maru ki War I
s: Religious life is presented as service to the Guru, remembrance of God's Name, humility, truthful conduct, and control of the passions. External dress, pilgrimage, silence, begging, and learned disputation do not constitute true religious life without love of God and the Word.

l: Hymns of Guru Nanak, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Bhairo
s: The unit concerns Bhairo's teaching that rituals, austerities, learning, pilgrimage, and religious dress are useless without God's name. It states that salvation is obtained through God's name and the Guru's instruction. It describes God as present in all creatures and says that Nanak drank God's elixir after stirring it. Man is portrayed as entangled in transmigration unless he repeats God's name.

l: Bhairo, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Bhairo
s: Bhairo teaches that offerings, penance, worship, learning, pilgrimage, religious dress, and bodily austerities are of no avail without God's name.

l: God, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Bhairo
s: God is in all creatures in the water, on dry land, in the nether regions, and in the firmament. The speaker asks God to preserve His servant by the favour of the Guru.

l: Guru, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Bhairo
s: The Guru's instruction is necessary for man to find salvation. The speaker asks for preservation through the Guru's favour.

l: Nanak, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Bhairo
s: Nanak stirred God's elixir and drank it.

l: the Name, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Bhairo
s: God's name is necessary for salvation and makes the holy man obtain it. Without it, birth, learning, religious practices, religious dress, and bodily austerities are useless, while whoever repeats it is saved.

l: salvation, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Bhairo
s: Salvation is not obtained without God's name. The unit also says that the Guru's instruction is necessary for salvation.

l: man, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Bhairo
s: Man dies an unprofitable death and wanders in transmigration without God's name. He may adopt religious practices, pilgrimage, austerities, or devotional dress, but he will not find comfort or satisfaction without the Name.

l: Hymns of Guru Nanak, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Basant
s: Rag Basant praises the great month in which spring begins and urges remembrance of the Sustainer of the earth. It teaches that pride should be subdued and that meditation on God and excellent virtues bring joy and spiritual wealth. The passage describes good acts, God's name, religion, divine knowledge, attainment of God, and dispelling mental pride through a tree metaphor. Nanak teaches that the pious who remain absorbed in God shall be perennial and never wither.

l: Rag Basant, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Basant
s: Rag Basant praises the month in which spring begins and urges remembrance of the Sustainer of the earth, meditation on God, and the adoption of excellent virtues.

l: God, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Basant
s: The Sustainer of the earth is to be remembered continually, and remembrance causes the heart to rejoice.

l: pride, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Basant
s: Pride is to be forgotten and subdued, while mental pride is to be dispelled through meditation on God.

l: virtue, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Basant
s: Good acts are described as the tree in a metaphor connecting spiritual practice with God's name, religion, divine knowledge, and attainment of God.

l: attainment of God, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Basant
s: Attainment of God is described as the fruit in the metaphor of good acts as a tree.

l: true merchandise, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Basant
s: The true Name is repeated with the tongue, and those who do so obtain the full wealth of honour and tranquilly meditate on God.

l: Nanak, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Basant
s: Nanak teaches that the pious who continue absorbed in God shall be perennial and never wither.

l: Hymns of Guru Nanak, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Sarang ki War
s: Sarang ki War teaches that impurity is not found in songs, knowledge, natural elements, or ablution, but in turning away from God. Nanak describes inner virtues and practices, including divine knowledge, continence, contentment, justice, meditation, mercy, forgiveness, truth, and good deeds. The unit criticizes idol worship, false wisdom, dishonest religious conduct, and gurus or pirs who beg, while praising those who earn honestly and give to others. It also teaches that God's will determines events and that God's name gives sight to the blind.

l: Sarang ki War, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Sarang ki War
s: Sarang ki War presents teachings about purity, wisdom, worship, truth, and right conduct. It condemns idol worship, dishonest religious behavior, and empty religious practices.

l: Nanak, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Sarang ki War
s: Nanak teaches that a person without a guru has no virtues and that turning away from God makes the mouth impure. He identifies divine knowledge, continence, contentment, alms, justice, meditation, truth, mercy, forgiveness, good deeds, and God's love as proper spiritual practices.

l: God, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Sarang ki War
s: God is described as having no partner and as being worthy of direct praise. What God and the Creator do comes to pass, and God favors those who follow the right way.

l: impurity, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Sarang ki War
s: Impurity is said not to exist in songs, knowledge, the phases of the moon or sun, corn, ablution, rain, earth, water, or air. The mouth of a person who turns away from God is described as impure.

l: divine knowledge, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Sarang ki War
s: Knowledge has no impurity and is used to understand what is read, worship the Lord, obtain honour, and properly give alms. Wisdom spent in wrangling is not true wisdom.

l: water, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Sarang ki War
s: Water is described as pure and as the generator of the world that will finally destroy everything. Drinking water quenches thirst but cannot wash the heart.

l: Guru, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Sarang ki War
s: A person without a guru is said to have no virtues. The unit warns against those who call themselves gurus and go begging.

l: idol, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Sarang ki War
s: An idol is washed, worshipped, offered kungu, sandal, and flowers, and addressed through ritual acts. Yet it does not give food to the hungry or preserve anyone from death.

l: the Name, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Sarang ki War
s: God's name gives sight to the blind. Writing God's name in order to sell it is condemned.

l: truth, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Sarang ki War
s: Truth is presented as a form of fasting and as part of the right spiritual way. Those without truth and modesty are said to receive no assistance hereafter.

l: contentment, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Sarang ki War
s: Contentment is described as a place of pilgrimage. It is also identified as one of the handfuls of water that is pure for the Brahman.

l: meditation, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Sarang ki War
s: Meditation on the True One is described as pure for the learned and as a form of ablution. Meditation on God is also presented as a cooking square and a proper spiritual practice.

l: right way, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Sarang ki War
s: The right way includes truth, contentment, divine knowledge, meditation, mercy, forgiveness, good deeds, God's love, and honest labour. Few people are said to make the right way their loincloths.

l: God's love, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Sarang ki War
s: God's love is described as food for those who follow the right spiritual way.

l: Hymns of Guru Nanak, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Malar .. Malar ki War
s: Rag Malar teaches that people should renounce covetousness, pride, slander, lust, wrath, and attachment to worldly distinctions, and should seek God through the Guru's instruction, God's name, and association with the saints. Malar Ashtapadi describes longing for the Beloved through images of the chakwi, lotus, chatrik, fish, and separated woman, teaching that God is found within through the Guru's favour. Malar ki War contrasts worldly bondage, transient wealth, beauty, nobility, and youth with liberation through recognizing the True One and the Word. Nanak praises God's name as the cooling remedy for the world's fire and blesses the means by which the True Name is written and divine knowledge is received.

l: Rag Malar, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Malar .. Malar ki War
s: Rag Malar teaches that people should shun covetousness, pride, evil inclinations, slander, lust, and wrath. It says that wisdom, knowledge, understanding, and lasting profit come from God's name, while love of God comes through association with the saints and instruction from the Guru.

l: Malar Ashtapadi, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Malar .. Malar ki War
s: Malar Ashtapadi portrays intense longing for the Beloved through the chakwi, lotus, chatrik, fish, and separated woman. It teaches that the Beloved is present within all, and that through the Guru's favour people find God in their hearts and become absorbed in Him.

l: Malar ki War, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Malar .. Malar ki War
s: Malar ki War teaches that prayers, worldly status, wealth, beauty, nobility, and youth cannot prevent death or bondage. It urges recognition of the True One and the Word, praises God's name as the cooling remedy for the world's fire, and blesses those connected with divine knowledge and the writing of the True Name.

l: God, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Malar .. Malar ki War
s: God is described as inaccessible and illimitable, dwelling in the human heart and placing eternal light within the body. God gives happiness, decides human fate, pervades every heart, frees those who recognize the True One, and blends with those on whom He looks with favour.

l: Guru, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Malar .. Malar ki War
s: The Guru gives God's name, precious instruction, and the words through which people receive spiritual teaching. The Guru's favour reveals God within, enables people to obtain the Beloved, and leads them toward absorption in Him.

l: Nanak, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Malar .. Malar ki War
s: Nanak teaches that the pious are invited to God's palace and will be blended with Him. He calls himself the dog of God's court, longs increasingly for God's love, asks only for God's name, and blesses the paper, pen, ink-bottle, ink, and writer who record the True Name.

l: men, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Malar .. Malar ki War
s: Humanity is warned against coveting others' wives and goods and against pride, evil inclinations, slander, lust, wrath, and worldly attachment. People are said to be subject to God's order and fate, but can find freedom by recognizing the True One, receiving the Guru's instruction, and finding God in their hearts.

l: the pious, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Malar .. Malar ki War
s: The pious are described as those who are absorbed in the True One and are known in God's court. They are invited to God's palace and will be blended with Him.

l: true merchandise, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Malar .. Malar ki War
s: God's name gives wisdom, knowledge, understanding, and day-and-night profit. It is the one thing Nanak asks for, and it cools the fire of the world.

l: the Word, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Malar .. Malar ki War
s: The Word is presented as the means by which people cross the terrible ocean. Recognizing it is part of the path to freedom from bondage and entry into the True One's court.

l: the heart, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Malar .. Malar ki War
s: The human heart is the place where the inaccessible and illimitable God dwells. Through the Guru's favour, people find God there, receive nectar, and have their burning extinguished.

l: world, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Malar .. Malar ki War
s: The world is described as transient like a flash of lightning and as a place of fire. Empire, wealth, beauty, nobility, and youth are called five robbers that have robbed the world, while God's name is said to cool its fire.

l: Hymns of Guru Nanak, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Prabhati .. Prabhati Ashtapadi
s: Rag Prabhati concerns Jogis, Sanyasis, Brahmans, the Word, the Guru, and devotion to God. It teaches that religious acts without knowledge of God are futile, while those tinctured by the Word become perfect Bairagis and are united with the True One. Prabhati Ashtapadi rejects yogic breath practices, ritual purification, austerities, and ceremonies when they are performed without the true Guru or repetition of the Name. It presents worldly desire, pride, false wisdom, and evil speech as sources of defilement, strife, and separation from God.

l: Rag Prabhati, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Prabhati .. Prabhati Ashtapadi
s: It describes Jogis, Sanyasis, Kaprias, Saravagis, and Brahmans, emphasizing that religious acts and learning are worthless without the Word and knowledge of God. It teaches that the true Guru unites man with God, ending sorrow, sin, and death.

l: Prabhati Ashtapadi, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Prabhati .. Prabhati Ashtapadi
s: It declares yogic breath-control practices, ritual washing, religious ceremonies, and other religious acts ineffective without the true Guru and repetition of the Name. It condemns worldly desire, pride, false wisdom, and evil speech as sources of impurity and strife.

l: Jogis, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Prabhati .. Prabhati Ashtapadi
s: They are said to go to ruin in twelve sects, and the Jogis, Kaprias, and plucked-headed Saravagis without the Word are described as having halters round their necks. Their breath-control practices are declared of no avail without the true Guru.

l: Nanak, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Prabhati .. Prabhati Ashtapadi
s: He teaches that if the true Guru is found, the Guru will unite man with God, so that sorrow, sin, and death will be no more.

l: God, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Prabhati .. Prabhati Ashtapadi
s: God is the one on whom love should be fixed, and from whom the perverse are separated. God is described as an ocean of merits, while worldly pursuit, impurity, pride, and the repetition of anything other than God's name are condemned.

l: God, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Prabhati .. Prabhati Ashtapadi
s: Those who love the jewel of the Name night and day are blended with the True One in every age.

l: Guru, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Prabhati .. Prabhati Ashtapadi
s: The true Guru gives instruction that makes people pure and worthy of honour at the true court. The true Guru unites man with God and leads him away from error, sorrow, sin, and death.

l: the Word, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Prabhati .. Prabhati Ashtapadi
s: Those tinctured by the Word become perfect Bairagis, and religious acts, purifications, austerities, devotion, penance, and pilgrimages abide in the Word. Without the Word, certain ascetics are described as having halters round their necks.

l: the Name, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Prabhati .. Prabhati Ashtapadi
s: The jewel of the Name is loved night and day, and repetition of the Name is presented as the only religious act that is not vain. The six religious duties are contained in the name of the Bright One.

l: religious ceremonies, Hymns of Guru Nanak, Rag Prabhati .. Prabhati Ashtapadi
s: They are said to be empty when performed without knowledge of God, and in Prabhati Ashtapadi they are called vain except for repetition of the Name. Purifications, austerities, devotion, penance, pilgrimages, ablutions, ceremonies, and decorations are rejected when they do not lead to God.

l: Additional Sloks of Guru Nanak, Additional Sloks of Guru Nanak, Additional Sloks of Guru Nanak
s: This unit concerns Nanak’s teachings on spiritual discernment, devotion, love, faith, and the conduct of religious and social groups. It urges people to reject evil, seek the True Guru, surrender themselves to divine love, and avoid attachment to transitory things and mammon. It defines the qualities of a true Brahman and Khatri, contrasts saints with deceitful and quarrelsome people, and recounts Ram Chandar’s mourning for Sita and Lachhman. It teaches that God is independent and that whatever the Perfect One does is complete and without deficiency.

l: Nanak, Additional Sloks of Guru Nanak, Additional Sloks of Guru Nanak
s: Nanak teaches people to examine their goods, reject evil, welcome good, and give themselves wholly to their friends. He declares that the world has lost companionship, love, and faith through mammon, praises those absorbed in God, and says that the pious who accept the Perfect One’s will shall be absorbed in Him.

l: God, Additional Sloks of Guru Nanak, Additional Sloks of Guru Nanak
s: God is described as Allwise, independent, and the one whose will determines whether a person becomes acceptable. Nanak teaches that God, rather than Ram, performed the deeds attributed to Ram, and that God’s actions and destiny cannot be erased.

l: True Guru, Additional Sloks of Guru Nanak, Additional Sloks of Guru Nanak
s: The True Guru protects those who address Him from fear amid the storms and waves of life. The Guru is also compared with a river of pilgrimage, making ablution pure for those who deem Him so.

l: love, Additional Sloks of Guru Nanak, Additional Sloks of Guru Nanak
s: Love among brethren and kinsmen has ceased in the world because of mammon. Divine love is compared to an arrow that, once shot by God, cannot be extracted, and Nanak urges people to give themselves to their friends through love.

l: faith, Additional Sloks of Guru Nanak, Additional Sloks of Guru Nanak
s: Faith has been lost on account of mammon. Nanak teaches that without faith there can be no meditation.

l: congregation of the saints, Additional Sloks of Guru Nanak, Additional Sloks of Guru Nanak
s: The congregation of the saints is to be congratulated. Nanak associates it with holy conduct and spiritual purity.

l: saints, Additional Sloks of Guru Nanak, Additional Sloks of Guru Nanak
s: The saints are described as few, while deceit and wrangling prevail in the world.

l: Brahman, Additional Sloks of Guru Nanak, Additional Sloks of Guru Nanak
s: A Brahman is one who knows God, performs devotion, penance, and self-restraint, and observes mildness and patience. Such a Brahman breaks his bonds, obtains salvation, and becomes worthy of worship.

l: Khatri, Additional Sloks of Guru Nanak, Additional Sloks of Guru Nanak
s: A Khatri is praised when he is brave in good deeds and uses his body in charity. A Khatri who examines his ground before giving gifts is acceptable in God’s court, while one who practices greed, covetousness, and falsehood suffers for his misdeeds.

l: Ram Chandar, Additional Sloks of Guru Nanak, Additional Sloks of Guru Nanak
s: Ram Chandar mourned inwardly for Sita and Lachhman and remembered Hanuman, who came to meet him. Nanak teaches that Ram Chandar could not erase his destiny because God is independent.

l: divine knowledge, Additional Sloks of Guru Nanak, Additional Sloks of Guru Nanak
s: Divine knowledge cannot be obtained without the Guru. The text also urges the person of divine knowledge to understand the allusion of the raven and the swan.

l: Japji
s: These passages from Japji describe a spiritual journey through divine realms and the limits of human speech about God. The first presents God, the True One, as the source of order, gifts, creation, judgment, knowledge, virtue, and salvation. Hearing and contemplating God’s Name, obeying God, and receiving the Guru’s instruction bring divine knowledge and spiritual benefit. It introduces the realms of righteousness, knowledge, and happiness; in the realm of knowledge divine light shines, songs yield countless joys, and incomparable beauty, wisdom, intellect, understanding, and supernatural skill are fashioned beyond adequate description. The next passage turns to the realm of action, marked by incomparable force, powerful warriors and heroes filled with Ram’s might, and many Sitas of indescribable beauty. Those with God in their hearts neither die nor go astray, while saints rejoice with the True One within them. God dwells in the true realm, favors its people, and beholds innumerable continents, worlds, universes, and forms performing their functions by God’s order. Nanak concludes that describing this vastness is impossible and emphasizes love for and meditation on God’s Name as a path to emancipation.

l: God, Japji
s: God is the True One and Creator: true, without fear or enmity, immortal, unborn, and self-existent by the Guru's favour. God gives gifts, establishes order, judges according to acts, and acts according to what pleases Himself. God dwells in the true realm, where God regards its denizens with favour and gives them happiness. Continents, worlds, universes, and forms carry out their functions according to God's orders; beholding and contemplating them, God is pleased. God’s greatness, works, and the worlds and forms cannot be fully described, and only God knows how great God is.

l: Guru, Japji
s: Guru is a guide who teaches that one Bestower gives to all living beings and that God is everywhere contained. It is identified with Shiv, Vishnu, Brahma, Parbati, Lakhshmi, and Saraswati. In the realm of knowledge, divine light, joy, beauty, incomparable fashioning, and knowledge, wisdom, intellect, understanding, and supernatural skill are described.

l: Nanak, Japji
s: Nanak is presented as teaching that people should live according to God's preordained will, avoid egoism, and accept whatever pleases God as good. The records describe realms in which divine knowledge brings joy, beauty marks the realm of happiness, and knowledge, wisdom, intellect, understanding, and supernatural skill are fashioned. What occurs there, as well as the continents, worlds, universes, and forms, cannot be completely described. The realm of action contains powerful warriors, heroes, saints, and those in whose hearts God dwells; they rejoice because the True One is in their hearts. God dwells in the true realm, looks on its denizens with favour, and makes them happy. The account closes with Nanak teaching that those who complete their toil and ponder on the Name may gain bright countenances and emancipation in the company of others.

l: God's Name, Japji
s: God's Name is presented as true, pure, and cleansing. Through love of the Name, it cleanses sin, removes sorrow and the mind's impurity, and is melted in divine love. It is also a true practice for those on whom God looks with favour. Within that practice, the Name is melted in divine love and the Word is coined in the true mint. Those who ponder the Name and depart after completing their toil may be emancipated. The account moves from the Name's truth and cleansing power, through its loving, favoured practice, to the possibility of emancipation for those who contemplate it.

l: God's order, Japji
s: God's order produces bodies and infuses souls, assigning greatness, status, pain, pleasure, reward, and transmigration to all without exemption. In the realm of knowledge, divine light, songs, beauty, incomparable fashioning, and fashioned wisdom and power appear. Understanding God's order removes egoism.

l: the Guru's instruction, Japji
s: The Guru's instruction reveals God's word and omnipresence. It guides people to hear and acquire divine knowledge, learn that God is everywhere contained, and understand that one Bestower sustains all living beings.

l: the realm of righteousness, Japji
s: The realm of righteousness is a realm where living beings are judged according to their acts. The elect are accepted and honoured, while the bad and the good are distinguished. It is described after the realm of knowledge, whose divine light, joys, beauty, and fashioned wisdom lead into this judgment.

l: the realm of knowledge, Japji
s: The realm of knowledge is a realm and a tool in spiritual practice. Its resplendent divine knowledge matters most, alongside fashioned knowledge, wisdom, intellect, understanding, and supernatural skill. It begins with light and songs yielding joys, moves through incomparable beauty and fashioning, and ends beyond description.

l: the realm of happiness, Japji
s: The realm of happiness is a realm characterized by beauty. It is a place where things are fashioned in an incomparable, indescribable manner, including knowledge, wisdom, intellect, understanding, and the skill of demigods and men of supernatural power.

l: the world, Japji
s: is_created_by God The world is laid out by the Commander according to His order. It contains countless worlds, lands, beings, forms, colours, species, and regions.

l: creation, Japji
s: is_a God's handiwork Creation is beyond counting and description, with countless worlds, beings, names, places, forms, and species. God created nights, seasons, lunar days, week days, wind, water, fire, and the earth as a temple.

l: Maya, Japji
s: gives_birth_to Brahma [in union with God] Maya, in union with God, gave birth to three children: one creator, one provider, and one destroyer. God directs them according to His orders and beholds them although they do not see Him.

l: congregations of saints, Japji
s: Congregations of saints are groups of saints who are ever happy, rejoicing with the True One in their hearts. They obtain salvation through hearing God's Name, which frees them from sorrow and sin. They ponder God's attributes and divine knowledge and sing God with love. They dwell in the true realm, within realms where divine knowledge, beauty, incomparable fashioning, force, and greatness are described. God dwells in the true realm, looks on its denizens with favour, and renders them happy. The account begins with their happiness and salvation through hearing God's Name, then places them amid divine knowledge and loving song, and ends with their dwelling and rejoicing in the true realm under God's favour.

l: the elect, Japji
s: The elect are acceptable, distinguished, and honoured in God's court, where they also shed lustre on kings' courts. They give their attention to the one Guru; the accompanying passage describes a realm of divine knowledge, joy, beauty, incomparable fashioning, and formed wisdom and understanding.

l: transmigration, Japji
s: is_governed_by God's order Transmigration occurs by God's order, and rebirth and deliverance depend on His will. Obeying God prevents a person from departing with Jam and from wandering in transmigration.

l: salvation, Japji
s: is_a gate Obeying God leads a person to the gate of salvation and saves him with his family. The Guru is saved and saves his disciples through obedience to God.

l: divine knowledge, Japji
s: Divine knowledge is a light in the realm of knowledge and an anvil in spiritual practice. Obtained through hearing God's Name, obeying God, and the Guru's instruction, it shines resplendently where songs yield joys, beauty prevails, and knowledge, wisdom, intellect, understanding, and supernatural skill are fashioned.

l: truth, Japji
s: is_a virtue God and His Name are true, and truth is associated with contentment and divine knowledge. A person becomes true before God by walking according to the will of the Commander.

l: sin, Japji
s: defiles the mind Sin defiles the mind, and the love of God's Name cleanses that impurity. People are judged according to their acts, and sorrow and sin disappear through hearing God's Name.

l: virtue, Japji
s: is_required_for devotion Virtue is formed through obedience to God and is associated with mercy and righteousness. All virtues belong to God, and no person can bestow virtue upon Him.

l: praise, Japji
s: is_unlimited without limit There is no limit to God's praises, and countless beings praise Him. Human descriptions cannot adequately express God's greatness, gifts, attributes, or deeds.

l: hearing God's Name, Japji
s: Hearing God's Name is an activity that grants truth, contentment, divine knowledge, honour, composure, and understanding. It removes sorrow and sin, and is compared with bathing at sixty-eight places of pilgrimage. It unfolds through hearing, then obtaining these qualities and release from sorrow and sin.

l: obedience to God, Japji
s: Obedience to God is an activity that produces wisdom and understanding and leads to salvation. It brings honour, ecstasy, virtue, freedom from punishment and transmigration, and the heart’s pleasure in His pure Name, unfolding through obedience into divine knowledge, fashioned intellect, and incomparable joy.

l: the court of God, Japji
s: The court of God is a court where the elect are accepted and honoured, while people are judged according to their acts. Its incomparable nature cannot be fully described. Recording angels write the record, and Dharmraj judges by it; there are also fashioned knowledge, wisdom, intellect, understanding, and supernatural skill.

l: realm of action, Japji
s: has_attribute force The realm of action is characterized by force. Its inhabitants are incomparable and include powerful warriors and heroes filled with the might of Ram, as well as many Sitas whose beauty cannot be described.

l: true realm, Japji
s: The true realm is where God dwells. God looks on its denizens with an eye of favor and renders them happy.

l: So Dar and So Purukh (the Rahiras)
s: Sodar and So Purukh present hymns by Guru Nanak, Guru Ram Das, and Guru Arjan praising God as eternal, supreme Creator, sovereign, and present in every heart. All beings and worlds sing His greatness, while He sustains creatures and determines events. Remembering and meditating on God’s true Name brings life, satisfaction, happiness, fearlessness, and liberation; forgetting it through worldly attachment brings misery and spiritual loss. The hymns urge service, the true Guru’s protection, saintly company, and using human life to meet God and cross the terrible ocean.

l: Sodar, So Dar and So Purukh (the Rahiras)
s: Sodar contains hymns concerning God’s greatness, His Name, creation, devotion, and the company of the saints.

l: Guru Nanak, So Dar and So Purukh (the Rahiras)
s: Guru Nanak is associated with Rag Asa. In Sodar, he portrays all creation praising God and teaches that remembering the true Name gives life. In So Purukh, he humbly seeks shelter, praises God as eternal Creator, and says God becomes manifest through the Guru's instruction.

l: God, So Dar and So Purukh (the Rahiras)
s: God is the one Supreme Being: eternal, immortal, pure, infinite, inaccessible, illimitable, fearless, omnipotent, and sovereign Lord and King of kings. God creates and sustains the world, continents, worlds, universe, and all creation, pervades everything, watches over all things, and provides daily bread for every creature. Possessing all treasures and eighteen supernatural powers, God knows all things and acts as He pleases. God gives grace and the jewel of God's name to those shown kindness, separates some from God and unites others with Himself. Through meditation, worship, and service, beings receive happiness, emancipation, freedom from fear, and absorption in God.

l: the true Lord, So Dar and So Purukh (the Rahiras)
s: is_a Lord [true] The true Lord is identified with the eternal and true God whose greatness cannot be fully described and whose Name is true.

l: God's name, So Dar and So Purukh (the Rahiras)
s: God's name is a jewel obtained through God's kindness. Remembering, cherishing, serving, and repeating it brings life, happiness, absorption, and relief from pain; forgetting it leaves people without spiritual worth, while repetition prepares them to cross the terrible ocean.

l: holy men, So Dar and So Purukh (the Rahiras)
s: Holy men meditate on, praise, and seek to please God through contemplation, study, worship, austerities, repetition, and duties; those who meditate abide in happiness and are emancipated from Death’s noose.

l: the universe, So Dar and So Purukh (the Rahiras)
s: is_supported_by God [by His hands] The universe is made and supported by God’s hands and is among the many things that sing His praises.

l: saints, So Dar and So Purukh (the Rahiras)
s: sings God [imbued with His love] Saints who please God and are imbued with His love sing His praises. Those who meet the saints are saved and come to know God’s attributes.

l: Guru Ram Das, So Dar and So Purukh (the Rahiras)
s: Guru Ram Das, associated with Rag Gujari, teaches servants, the true Guru, and saints to supplicate and meditate on God, seek enlightenment through His Name, and serve Him. The company of saints reveals God’s attributes; pleasing God brings happiness, emancipation, fearlessness, and absorption in the Supreme Being within every heart.

l: the true Guru, So Dar and So Purukh (the Rahiras)
s: The true Guru mercifully protects seekers, instructs them in God’s Name, enlightens their souls, and blesses those who enter its protection and society.

l: the company of the saints, So Dar and So Purukh (the Rahiras)
s: The company of the saints blesses those who meet it by revealing God’s attributes and bringing salvation through God’s favor.

l: Guru Arjan, So Dar and So Purukh (the Rahiras)
s: Guru Arjan is associated with Rag Gujari and teaches trust in God’s provision. He presents human life as a chance to meet God, urges fellowship with saints and repetition of God’s name, and humbly seeks preservation despite base actions.

l: God's praises, So Dar and So Purukh (the Rahiras)
s: is_an_occupation singing [for the speaker] God’s praises are sung by wind, water, fire, divine beings, holy men, heroes, singers, creatures, and the worlds. His praises are beyond complete enumeration or description.

l: humanity, So Dar and So Purukh (the Rahiras)
s: Humanity is a helpless, God-forgetful creature entangled in worldly love, given a human body and roles in God’s play; it should join saints, repeat God’s name, meet God, and cross the terrible ocean.

l: creation, So Dar and So Purukh (the Rahiras)
s: disappears when created God fashioned the whole creation, and everything made belongs to God. Creation is described as God's play, with all living creatures contained in God, though what has been created will eventually disappear.

l: worldly love, So Dar and So Purukh (the Rahiras)
s: Worldly love is a mire causing misery, vain life, forgetfulness, melted virtues, and drowning that prevents humanity from thinking of God.

l: Sohila (Kirtan Sohila)
s: This collection of hymns centers on praise of the one Creator, remembrance of God, and refuge in the Guru and saints. Guru Nanak begins with Sohila: in a house filled with God’s praise, the soul-bride awaits her Lord as the day of the Caller approaches. He then affirms that, despite many philosophical schools, teachers, doctrines, seasons, and forms, the Guru of gurus and God are one. A cosmic worship follows, with sun, moon, stars, wind, forests, and fragrance offered to the divine light present in all things; the speaker longs for God’s lotus feet and the Name. Guru Ram Das presents saints as those absorbed in God’s love and Name, whose company destroys lust and wrath and frees people from transmigration, while pride brings pain and death. Guru Arjan closes by urging service to the saints, meeting the Guru before life passes, and receiving God’s word. Those awakened by God understand the Ineffable, attain peace, and escape return to the world.

l: Guru Nanak, Sohila (Kirtan Sohila)
s: Guru Nanak is portrayed as a devoted servant focused on God. He teaches remembrance of the Caller, the oneness of God despite many forms, cosmic worship, and God’s light in everything. His account moves from teaching toward intimate devotion: longing for God’s lotus feet, seeking favour to dwell in God’s name, finding happiness there, and calling himself a slave who desires the saints’ feet-dust.

l: Rag Gauri Dipaki, Sohila (Kirtan Sohila)
s: is_a rag Rag Gauri Dipaki presents teachings about singing the Sohila, praising God, and awaiting the Lord. It describes marriage preparations and urges remembrance of the approaching day.

l: God, Sohila (Kirtan Sohila)
s: God is the one Creator, Giver, fearless Lord, Searcher of hearts, and Arranger, with many forms yet no single form or organ. Praised and meditated on in the house, God watches over living things and regards their wants. God’s worship gathers sun, moon, firmament, stars, sandal perfume, wind, forests, and ecstatic strains; light is in everything, and what pleases God is real. God destroys birth and is the greatest of the great, preserving the poor and wretched. By God’s favour, people awaken, drink the essence of God’s word, know the Ineffable, receive God in the heart, and gain a home in God’s palace.

l: Sohila, Sohila (Kirtan Sohila)
s: Sohila is a song of joy sung in the house where God's praise is sung and He is meditated on, providing everlasting comfort.

l: speaker (the bride), Sohila (Kirtan Sohila)
s: A bride, prepared through recorded marriage rites and supported by relations, asks friends to pray that she may meet God.

l: six schools of philosophy, Sohila (Kirtan Sohila)
s: Six schools of philosophy, each with a teacher and doctrine, are described together.

l: system in which the Creator is praised, Sohila (Kirtan Sohila)
s: praises Creator The system in which the Creator is praised should be preserved, and doing so will redound to the father's glory.

l: worship, Sohila (Kirtan Sohila)
s: Worship consists of the cosmos itself: the sun and moon are lamps, the firmament is a salver, the stars are pearls, sandal perfume is incense, the wind is a fan, and the forests are flowers. What pleases God is identified as real worship.

l: light, Sohila (Kirtan Sohila)
s: God's light fills and makes everything brilliant; the Guru's teaching manifests this light.

l: God's name, Sohila (Kirtan Sohila)
s: God's name supports Nanak, brings happiness through absorption, and is presented as a profit people should earn in this life.

l: Guru Ram Das, Sohila (Kirtan Sohila)
s: is_found_by predestination Guru Ram Das teaches that meeting the saints destroys lust and wrath. He praises reverence toward the saints and warns against the suffering caused by pride.

l: the saints of God, Sohila (Kirtan Sohila)
s: The saints of God are absorbed in the Name, having destroyed pain and fear of transmigration and found God, the imperishable Being. Honoured across earth and universe, they are served by people; becoming dust of their feet is a source of happiness.

l: transmigration, Sohila (Kirtan Sohila)
s: The saints of God have destroyed the pain and fear associated with transmigration.

l: happiness, Sohila (Kirtan Sohila)
s: Happiness is promised in the next world and in God's palace, and Nanak craves it through becoming the dust of the saints' feet.

l: Guru Arjan, Sohila (Kirtan Sohila)
s: is_in_rag Rag Gauri Purbi Guru Arjan urges people to serve the saints, earn God's name, meet the Guru, and arrange their affairs. He teaches that by the Guru's favour God will dwell in the heart.

l: human life, Sohila (Kirtan Sohila)
s: grows_shorter every day and night Human life grows shorter every day and night, so people are urged to meet the Guru and arrange their affairs.
